h1:
Koh Mak Couples Itinerary
Quiet Beaches — Seaside Dinners — Sunsets
intro: Koh Mak sits between Koh Chang and Koh Kood in Trat province. It's small, shaped a bit like a four-pointed star, and there are no clubs and no noisy walking streets here — just quiet beaches, leaning coconut palms, and clear water. It's an island for couples who want to slip away from the crowds and have a few slow days to themselves. We built this plan around quiet beaches, dinners by the sea, and ending every day with a sunset, and it works as a 2-day, 1-night trip or a 3-day, 2-night one.

blocks.html: Before you plan, know that Koh Mak is farther out than a lot of the islands near Bangkok. You take a car to Laem Ngop pier in Trat, then a boat for about 45 minutes more. The upside of that distance is fewer people — the island stays calm and most beaches are nearly empty. It suits anyone who actually wants privacy.

Koh Mak is small enough to loop on a bicycle or one of the electric scooters the resorts rent out. The island's main beaches are Ao Kao in the southwest and Ao Suan Yai in the northwest. Both face west, so you get the sunset from either one — which is why this plan catches both beaches at the time the light is best.

blocks.title: What to know before you go (honesty)
blocks.html: A lot of Koh Mak shuts down during monsoon season, roughly May to October. Some resorts, restaurants, and boat operators stop running, the sea gets choppy, and rain comes in heavy spells. The best window is November to April. · Everything on the island costs more than on the mainland because it has to come over by boat. ATMs are few and sometimes run out of cash, so bring enough cash with you. · If you're diving or taking a boat out, always check the weather first. · Koh Mak markets itself as a low-carbon destination — carry your trash back and don't step on the coral.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Arrive, settle into a quiet beach, end with cocktails on the pier for the sunset

blocks.html: Day one is mostly about getting to the island, checking into a beachfront stay, and then sinking into a quiet beach all afternoon with nowhere to be. Close the day with a cocktail at the pier bar, timed right for sunset.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Arrive — quiet beach — sunset off the pier

items.activity: Leave Laem Ngop, take the speedboat across to Koh Mak
items.note: The speedboat from Laem Ngop pier takes about 45 minutes and runs around 450 THB per person each way (the ferry is cheaper but slower). There are morning and midday departures — book ahead in high season. The boat drops you at your resort's pier on the island.

items.activity: Check into a beachfront stay, rent a bicycle or electric scooter
items.note: Basing yourself around Ao Kao or Ao Suan Yai is the most convenient. Most resorts rent bikes by the day. The island roads are narrow and quiet, so even a slow ride loops the whole island easily.

items.activity: Lunch at a roadside spot behind Ao Kao
items.note: The road behind Ao Kao beach is lined with small Thai eateries and made-to-order shops, cheaper than the resorts. A relaxed, easy-on-the-wallet first meal before you hit the beach.

The main beach in the southwest — white sand, clear water, a row of leaning palms. It's the liveliest beach on the island but still never packed, good for reading, swimming, or some easy snorkeling along the shore.

items.activity: Ride along the coast and find a quiet corner for photos
items.note: Koh Mak hides several small beaches, like Ao Tao Khai, which was once a turtle-nesting spot — quiet, with very few people. A nice stop for photos before the evening light.

items.activity: Cocktails at the Koh Mak Cococape pier bar for sunset
items.note: Cococape Resort has a small bar at the end of a pier that runs out over the water. There's a happy hour in the evening — sip a drink and watch the sun slowly drop below the horizon to the west. It's a romantic corner couples love to settle into.

items.activity: First dinner on Ao Kao beach
items.note: Several Ao Kao resorts set dinner tables right on the sand, with Thai food and seafood. Check prices before you order — island prices run higher than the mainland. Keep it light tonight; the first day's travel is tiring.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Kayak to Koh Kham, Ao Suan Yai, and a seaside dinner with the sunset

blocks.html: Day two is the highlight of a couples' trip. In the morning you head out to Koh Kham, the little island just off Koh Mak; in the afternoon you move over to Ao Suan Yai, where the white sand runs for a kilometer; then you close the day with a beachfront dinner and a full, unobstructed sunset.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Koh Kham — Ao Suan Yai — seaside dinner

items.activity: Take a boat or kayak out to Koh Kham
items.note: Koh Kham is a small island off Ao Suan Yai, about 5–10 minutes by boat from the pier, around 300 THB. It has white sand and clear water, good for swimming and snorkeling over the shallow coral. Always check the swell before you head out.

items.activity: Back to Koh Mak for a light lunch
items.note: Head back, change, and grab lunch at a café or a spot near your stay. Midday sun is strong — rest in the shade before heading back out to the beach in the afternoon.

items.activity: Laze on Ao Suan Yai beach
items.note: The northwest beach, white sand running about 2 km, with shallow water you can wade out a long way. Quieter than Ao Kao, with views of Koh Kham and Koh Kradat off in the distance — a spot couples like to just sit in.

items.activity: Head up to the Seavana rooftop for the breeze before sunset
items.note: Seavana Koh Mak Beach Resort at Ao Suan Yai has a rooftop and pool bar with a lovely sunset view. There's an evening happy hour — sip a drink as the golden light slowly shifts color.

items.activity: Seaside dinner at Ao Suan Yai, with the sunset
items.note: Ao Suan Yai is known for its beachfront restaurants where you eat as the sun drops into the sea. There's Thai and Western food — order fresh seafood or a single dish. Reserving a seaside table ahead is the safer bet in high season.

blocks.title: Sunset-spot tips
blocks.html: Because Koh Mak is shaped like a star, you can pick a different angle on the sunset each evening. First night, take the pier bar at Ao Kao; second night, Ao Suan Yai. If you have a third night, try Ao Pra — the quietest beach with the fewest people, ideal if you want full privacy. The sunsets on Koh Mak are best on clear-sky days, November through February.

blocks.text: If you have a third night — add a spa, a workshop, and a quiet bay

blocks.html: If you stay 3 days and 2 nights, there's no rush on the last day. Take it slow with easy things you do together, before catching the afternoon boat back to the mainland.

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: An easy day before heading home

items.activity: Take a Thai cooking class together at Smile Cooking School
items.note: A Thai cooking class in the Ao Nid area, four dishes, around 1,500 THB per person, with morning and afternoon sessions. A fun thing to do as a couple — and you go home full.

items.activity: Unwind with a spa session or a massage by the sea
items.note: Several resorts, Seavana included, offer beachside massage and spa treatments. A Thai or oil massage to loosen up before the trip home. Book a slot ahead when it's busy.

items.activity: Stop by Ao Pra for one last quiet corner
items.note: Ao Pra is the quietest bay on the island, usually just locals fishing. Good for a walk and a few photos of the two of you with no one around before you leave.

items.activity: Pack up, take the boat back to Laem Ngop
items.note: Check return boat times with your stay in advance, leaving room to carry on to Trat town or back to Bangkok. In high season the boats fill fast — book your return ticket when you first arrive.

blocks.text: Seaside dinners and sunset bars couples love

blocks.html: Koh Mak doesn't have a dense eating-and-drinking strip like the bigger islands — the spots are scattered across the resorts and along the beaches. We picked the dinner corners and bars that are actually open and popular with couples, ordered by how romantic the seaside setting is.

items.name: Koh Mak Cococape pier bar
items.blurb: A small cocktail bar at the end of a pier running out over the water at Ao Kao. Dangle your feet, sip a drink, and watch the sun drop into the sea with nothing in the way. It's the corner couples photograph the most on the island.

items.name: Beachfront dinner at Ao Suan Yai
items.blurb: The beachfront restaurants along Ao Suan Yai set tables right on the sand so you eat as the sun drops into the sea. There's Thai food, fresh seafood, and Western dishes, and it's quieter than the Ao Kao side.
items.meta: Ao Suan Yai · book a seaside table ahead in high season
items.price: Single dishes around ฿120–200 · seafood by weight

items.name: Seavana pool bar and rooftop
items.blurb: Seavana Koh Mak Beach Resort at Ao Suan Yai has a poolside bar and a rooftop with a lovely sunset view. Happy-hour cocktails with an open sea view.
items.meta: Ao Suan Yai · pool bar + rooftop

items.name: Banana Sunset Bar
items.blurb: An easygoing beach bar on the Ao Kao side, with live music some nights. Sit and chill with the sea breeze and watch the sun set over the Gulf of Thailand — good for couples who want to settle in for a long evening.
items.meta: Ao Kao · live music some nights

items.name: Beachfront resort restaurants at Ao Kao
items.blurb: Several Ao Kao resorts lay out dinner on the sand, so you eat under string lights with the sound of the waves. Both seafood and Thai food — good for a special meal for two on the first night, when you don't want to travel far yet.
items.meta: Ao Kao · dinner on the sand
items.price: A meal for two around ฿500–1,200 depending on the menu

items.name: Seaside café at Ao Kao
items.blurb: By day there's a beachfront café for a coffee and a snack out of the sun. Quiet atmosphere, good for a long chat or reading while you wait for the light to soften.

blocks.html: The prices above are rough ranges from the latest information and can change with the season and the menu. Things on the island generally cost more than the mainland because they have to come over by boat — ask the price before you order, every time, and carry cash since many places only take cash.

items: Boat to the island (Laem Ngop–Koh Mak) — speedboat around ฿450/person each way (about 45 min) · the ferry is cheaper but takes longer
Boat to Koh Kham — around ฿300/trip, about 5–10 min from Ao Suan Yai (or paddle a kayak yourself if the water's calm)
Vehicle rental on the island — motorbike/electric scooter around ฿250–400/day · a bicycle is cheaper and enough to loop the island
Thai cooking class at Smile Cooking School — around ฿1,500/person, four dishes
Meals — roadside dishes around ฿80–150 each · beachfront dinners/seafood cost more, check the price before you order
Cash — ATMs on the island are few and sometimes out of cash, so bring enough for the whole trip

faq.q: How many days do you need for a couples' trip to Koh Mak?
faq.a: 2 days and 1 night covers the main beaches, but if you want to take it slow with no rush, 3 days and 2 nights is about right. Day one, do Ao Kao beach and the sunset off the pier; day two, Koh Kham and a seaside dinner at Ao Suan Yai; day three, add a cooking class and a spa before you head home.

faq.q: Which beach on Koh Mak is quietest and best for couples?
faq.a: Ao Suan Yai in the northwest is quiet, with white sand running about 2 km and beachfront dinner spots for the sunset. Ao Pra is the quietest bay of all, usually just locals fishing — ideal if you want full privacy. Ao Kao is livelier but still never packed.

faq.q: When's the best time to visit Koh Mak, and what should you avoid?
faq.a: The best window is November to April — clear skies, calm sea, beautiful sunsets. Avoid the monsoon season, roughly May to October, when some resorts, restaurants, and boat operators stop running, the sea gets choppy, and rain comes in heavy spells.

faq.q: Can you use cards on Koh Mak, or should you bring cash?
faq.a: Bring enough cash for the whole trip. ATMs on the island are few and sometimes run out of cash, and many shops and services only take cash. Things on the island also cost more than the mainland because everything comes over by boat.

faq.q: Where's the best place to watch the sunset on Koh Mak?
faq.a: Koh Mak is shaped like a star, so the west-facing beaches give you several sunset spots. The popular ones are the pier bar at Ao Kao, the rooftop and pool bar at Ao Suan Yai, and Banana Sunset Bar. If you want the quietest spot, go to Ao Pra. The sunsets are best on clear-sky days, November through February.
